title: Source follower
description: A source follower (common-drain buffer): the drain sits at VDD, the source drives the load, and the output tracks the input one gate-source drop below it. The voltage gain Av = gm/(gm + gds + 1/R_L) is just under unity and the output resistance is about 1/gm, so this stage buffers a high-impedance node into a resistive load R_L without voltage gain. The DC level shift is one vgs: V_out = V_in - vgs. vgs is not known before sizing, so vgs_est places the operating point and the level-shift-consistent guardrail checks it against the reported vgs; retune vgs_est until green. The body is assumed tied to the source (vsb = 0), so no body effect appears and gmb - which is not on every table - is deliberately omitted.

params.name: V_in
params.note: input DC level; the output sits one vgs below it

params.name: R_L
params.note: load resistance at the source; may be large (a light load approaches Av -> gm/(gm+gds))

params.name: gm_id
params.note: higher gm/ID raises gm (gain closer to 1, lower Rout) at the cost of headroom

params.name: vgs_est
params.note: estimate of the follower vgs, used to place the drain-source bias VDD - V_out; retune until the level-shift-consistent guardrail is green

rows.name: V_out
rows.note: the DC level shift: the output is one gate-source drop below the input

rows.name: Av
rows.note: follower gain, below unity; gmb is omitted (body tied to source)

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: output resistance, about 1/gm for a light load

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: input-referred channel thermal density; the near-unity gain passes it through with little change

rules.note: gm/ID cannot exceed the weak-inversion ceiling of the data
device saturated: the drain-to-source voltage is VDD minus the source (output) level
the biasing vgs_est should match the reported vgs; retune it if this trips
